name: PT Sanurhasta Mitra Tbk

frontmatter.title: Sanurhasta Mitra: land bank, cash box and the konglo premium
frontmatter.summary: MINA is a Bali land bank and villa operator controlled by the Hapsoro group. Value sits in cash and a Sanur parcel appraised far above book, now bridged at four-fifths of the tax-office value for its HGB tenure and the absent permit. The going-concern note and a police case naming a shareholder sit against the premium the konglo lens preserves.
thesis: The operating company is a cost centre: gross profit does not cover head-office cost, and the result depends on deposit interest on rights-issue cash [S4].
The asset base is sourced: cash after the 2025 rights issue, a Sanur land bank carried at cost and appraised by the tax office at many times that, and Boyolali housing land at book [S3][S4].
We bridge Sanur at four-fifths of the tax-office value, not all of it: the HGB titles have roughly eighteen years left and no permit, partner or pre-sales exist [S4].

The audited accounts carry a going-concern material-uncertainty paragraph, and the police case names a suspect as a MINA shareholder and the villa operator leases its land from that suspect's wife, who was declared bankrupt [S3][S6].
The market pays a large premium to that asset value; the konglo lens, not the business, decides how much of the premium survives twelve months, with the MSCI decision inside the window [S5].

catalysts.event: IDX minimum free-float step of fifteen per cent takes effect for large caps already in the twelve-and-a-half to fifteen per cent band; MINA, a small cap, faces its own step only at the end of March 2029 and already clears it
MSCI consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone status closes for feedback
MSCI announces its reclassification decision for Indonesia, inside our twelve-month window
FY2026 audited accounts: whether the Sanur scheme has a contract, permit, JV partner or pre-sales, and whether the going-concern paragraph repeats

blocks.text: **REDUCE**, target Rp146 against a price of 169.0 (-13.7%). The fundamental twelve-month value is Rp63; the difference is the konglo lens, which keeps part of a large price-to-value premium for another year rather than closing it at once, as set out in the house konglo regime deck rather than by any third-party view.

The company is a small Bali property and hospitality shell. It owns a villa estate in Umalas through The Santai, a beachfront land bank in Sanur held as investment property, and housing land in Boyolali held as inventory; it also holds the proceeds of a 2025 rights issue in deposits [S3][S4]. The trading business does not pay for itself. Gross profit is smaller than the head-office cost, so the operating line is negative in every year of the history, and the reported bottom line depends on interest income from the deposit book [S0][S4]. We therefore value what the company owns, not a stream of earnings it does not produce.

The asset values are sourced rather than asserted. The Sanur parcel is carried at IDR65.4bn in the investment-property note while the same note discloses a tax-office fair value of IDR533.7bn, several times the carrying amount and with HGB titles expiring between 2044 and 2045 [S4]. We mark the parcel at four-fifths of that appraisal in the bridge, because a tax-office assessment is not a transaction price, no permit or partner exists, and the titles are finite. The Boyolali housing land sits in inventory at IDR23.6bn, for which no appraisal exists, so we keep book and flag the asymmetry [S4]. Cash and equivalents reached IDR162.7bn at the end of the last financial year, after the rights issue that raised IDR164.0bn [S3][S4]. Those items, less the present value of the operating losses the shell keeps incurring, are our fundamental value.

Three things move the value. First, the Sanur scheme. The board appointed Lab Architecture Bureau under cooperation agreements dated 16 June 2025 and 8 August 2025, and the work stands at schematic-design finalisation; no construction contract, permit, joint venture or pre-sales have been disclosed [S3]. A signed development partner is worth more than raw land; another year of delay costs another year of overhead and brings the HGB expiry closer. Second, the konglo regime. The price sits at a large premium to fundamental value, and the house lens closes only part of that gap within twelve months, with the MSCI reclassification decision due by 30 June 2027 inside the window [S5]. Third, governance. Control changed in 2025 through a mandatory tender offer, the shares were suspended six times in that year for cumulative price rises, the audited accounts carry a going-concern material-uncertainty paragraph, and the police case names one of its suspects as a MINA shareholder and the villa operator leases its land from that suspect's wife, who was declared bankrupt [S3][S6].

The variant view is that the market is pricing a development that has not started and a group that has not committed capital to it, while the underlying land and cash are real and disclosed. The risk to that view is not the operating business - it is a second equity raise, a related-party asset transaction, or a regime event that removes the passive demand supporting premium valuations across the complex [S5][S7].

Indonesian listed property shells often trade on the value of their land rather than on earnings, because land in Bali has appreciated faster than the operating business has compounded. The market also attaches a premium to vehicles controlled by large family groups, on the expectation that the group will inject assets or capital into the listed entity.

Sanurhasta Mitra is a property and hospitality company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange since 2017 [S3]. It runs three things: a boutique villa property called The Santai in Umalas, Bali, with 11.0 units in private-pool villas; a subsidised housing project through its subsidiary Sanur Hasta Griya in Boyolali, Central Java, still at the study stage; and a land bank in Sanur, Bali, of 37,100 m2 held for future commercial or health-tourism development [S3][S4]. It employs a small head-office team and does not report a segment split, which tells you how small the operating business is relative to the balance sheet [S3].

The revenue base is the villa estate. The Santai contributes the bulk of consolidated revenue [S3]. Housing sales are not yet a revenue line; management describes the Boyolali land as being studied for its highest and best use [S3]. The Sanur land produces no rent at all, as the investment-property note states explicitly [S4]. Consolidated revenue for the last financial year was IDR9.0bn, up 8.0% on the prior year, and the first nine months of the current year came in slightly below the same period a year earlier [S4].

Ownership and control changed in 2025. The ultimate beneficial owner is Happy Hapsoro, who became controller after his direct and indirect holdings passed half of the company; the parent entity is PT Tirta Orisa Yasa [S3]. The Hapsoro group's other listed vehicles named by the press are RAJA, RATU, PADI, BUVA and UANG, spanning gas and energy infrastructure, upstream oil and gas, securities, villas and land [S8]. This vehicle is the group's Bali property arm: the listed holder of the Sanur land bank and the villa estate. A rights issue completed in mid-2025 raised Rp164,000,000,000 and diluted earlier holders [S3]. Management describes the proceeds as supporting business development, operational strengthening and strategic investment, with the Sanur land development named as the focus [S3].

Strategy, in management's own words, is to convert the Sanur site into an integrated destination of international standard while keeping the villa estate as the stable operating asset and the Boyolali land as a longer-dated housing pipeline [S3]. A new president director took over at the start of 2026, presented as the step to accelerate the three segments [S3]. The appointment of Lab Architecture Bureau, on cooperation agreements dated 16 June 2025 and 8 August 2025 and now at schematic-design finalisation, is the only concrete development step disclosed to date; there is no budget, timetable or funding plan attached to it [S3].

The group structure matters for how the asset will be monetised. The controller holds a little under a third through the parent, a further fifth directly, and the free float is dispersed across holders each below the five per cent threshold [S3]. Decisions on the Sanur site, on any further capital raise and on related-party transactions therefore rest with the controller, and minority holders are price-takers on the timing of value realisation.

Bali's Sanur area has been designated a health special economic zone, which allows healthcare and wellness operators to build there with fiscal incentives. That designation is why a land parcel in the district can be worth more as a development site than as an empty plot.

The relevant market is Bali boutique hospitality plus Bali land, and neither is a scale business for this company. Boutique villa supply in the Umalas and Seminyak corridor is fragmented across hundreds of small operators, and the competitive variable is seasonal occupancy and nightly rate rather than share [S3]. The company's own risk section names intense competition in Bali property and hospitality and fluctuating tourism trends that affect occupancy and property values as its principal operating risks [S3]. It mitigates by differentiating on the boutique-resort concept and by exploring the land bank [S3].

On the property side the company is a challenger with a single strategic parcel rather than a developer with a pipeline. Its own description of the Sanur asset is a land bank of 37,100 m2 on the beachfront, positioned inside the health-zone development area, intended for mixed-use or health-tourism facilities [S3][S4]. That is a site-specific option, not a franchise: there is no disclosed market share in Bali villa supply, no branded management contract of its own, and no construction track record in the current ownership era [S3].

The regulatory and market-regime layer matters more than the industry layer for the share price. The exchange now publishes a high-shareholding-concentration list, which stood at eighty-two issuers in late October, and names on that list are excluded from the main index calculation [S7]. The index provider has frozen increases for Indonesian securities and opened a consultation on reclassifying the country to standalone status, with a decision due by the middle of 2027 [S5]. The fifteen per cent minimum free-float rule is being phased in by market-cap band: issuers above five trillion rupiah already inside the twelve-and-a-half to fifteen per cent band must reach fifteen per cent by the end of March 2027, larger caps below that band by the end of March 2028, and issuers below five trillion rupiah by the end of March 2029 [S9]. MINA is not on the concentration list and reports a compliant float of 44.5% against the fifteen per cent threshold, so its own deadline does not bind [S3][S7][S9].

Five forces, briefly. Supplier power is low, because the villa estate buys local services. Buyer power is high in the sense that guests and villa buyers are price-sensitive and can substitute across the island. New entrants are many in villas but few for beachfront land, the one genuinely scarce input. Substitutes are strong in hospitality, and rivalry is intense and cyclical. The moat, if any, is the land title rather than the operating business, and that moat is only worth its appraised value if a permit and a partner arrive [S4].

The macro overlay is a caution flag rather than a driver. The house macro desk has Indonesian rate-sensitive consumer names on avoid, and this company's reported profit depends on deposit rates, so a falling rate cycle reduces the interest income that currently covers the overhead [S4]. Tourism arrivals are the other external variable; they are not modelled explicitly because the villa estate is capacity-bound at 11.0 units [S3].

On the external-influence side, the property and hospitality sector in Bali is exposed to tourism policy, visa rules and land-use regulation in the health zone, none of which the company quantifies [S3]. We do not model any of them as a base-case drift; they sit in the bear case and in the signposts we monitor.

Boutique villas in Bali are usually owned by individuals or small companies and managed by specialist operators. The economics are driven by occupancy in the June-to-September and December-to-January peaks, and by the villa's ability to command a premium for privacy and private pools.

Revenue has moved in a narrow band for four years: IDR9.3bn, IDR11.7bn, IDR8.3bn and IDR9.0bn [S0]. Gross margin has stayed in the sixties as a percentage of revenue, at 63.5%, because the mix is villa room revenue with direct costs near a third of sales [S3][S4]. What has not stayed stable is the cost base: selling and administrative expenses exceed gross profit, so EBITDA has been negative in every year of the history, at IDR-0.3bn, IDR-0.5bn, IDR-3.7bn and IDR-3.0bn (the minus signs are losses) [S0]. The reported net result has been less bad than the operating result because interest income and one-off items sit below the line; net profit to parent was IDR-5.6bn and IDR-2.9bn in the last two years [S0].

The balance sheet changed shape in 2025. Cash and equivalents reached IDR162.7bn at the year-end after the rights issue, from a negligible base a year earlier [S4]. There is no bank debt; the only borrowings are small lease liabilities of IDR0.1bn [S4]. Net debt is therefore strongly negative at IDR-162.6bn, and we forecast it to stay negative through the horizon as interest income accumulates on the deposit book [S0]. Investment property is carried at cost of IDR65.4bn against a tax-office fair value of IDR533.7bn [S4]. Inventory of housing land is IDR23.6bn, and operating working capital is about one and a half times revenue at the last balance sheet; we hold that ratio into the forecast, so the model books no one-off working-capital release when it rolls from the actual year into the first forecast year [S0][S4].

Our forecast keeps the business where it is. Revenue is flat this year, because the nine-month actual is below the prior year and the villa estate cannot add rooms without capex, then grows at a low single-digit rate [S4]. Gross margin is held at the last actual. Overhead is held at the last actual ratio, which is above gross margin, so EBITDA stays negative at IDR-3.0bn this year and IDR-3.0bn next [S0]. Free cash flow to the firm is negative in every forecast year, at IDR-3.1bn this year, because the operating loss and the working-capital build exceed depreciation and maintenance capex; the first forecast year no longer carries the working-capital release that an unsupported lower ratio would have manufactured [S0][S4]. The bottom line turns positive only because of interest income on the deposit book, at IDR2.1bn this year [S0]. We assume no dividend and no share issuance; both would be events, not base-case assumptions.

Earnings quality. The accruals picture is dominated by the cash raise rather than by working capital, so the usual accrual ratio is not informative this year; what matters is that operating cash flow was negative in the last reported year and that the operating loss is real [S0][S4]. Receivables are trivial relative to revenue, so there is no channel-stuffing signal. Inventory has not been written up. The genuine quality flags are elsewhere. The result depends on interest income rather than operations, which means the profit line moves with deposit rates and with the size of the cash pile, not with the business. Investment property is carried at cost with a very large gap to appraised value, which is conservative for the balance sheet but means reported book equity tells you little about asset value [S4]. And the rights issue was raised without a disclosed project budget or timetable [S3]. We treat the land value as the primary asset and the operating business as a cost to be deducted.

We restate rather than model around the data pack where it matters. The pack's history is internally consistent with the audited accounts on revenue and the operating result, and the key balance-sheet lines - cash, investment property, inventory - are keyed to the audited note figures as facts, so the engine builds its history from the filing [S4]. The one line we do not take from the pack at face value is depreciation, which is small in absolute terms and immaterial to the valuation given that the operating component is negative before it [S0].

Capital allocation. The company has no dividend record, no buyback and no disclosed capex programme beyond maintenance of IDR0.1bn [S3][S0]. The rights-issue cash sits in deposits, earning IDR6.2bn at our modelled deposit yield [S0]. That is rational only if the development proceeds; if it does not, the cash earns a deposit rate while the overhead consumes part of it, which is what our forecast shows. Related-party flows are not disclosed as material, and no supplier transaction exceeds a tenth of consolidated revenue [S3].

Indonesian property companies often carry land at historical cost for decades, so a balance sheet at book value can understate the market value of the land substantially. Analysts typically revalue the land to a market or tax-office benchmark before comparing the company with its share price.

We use a discounted cash flow of the operating business with every non-operating asset added explicitly, because the earnings-based methods do not apply. EBITDA is negative, so an EV/EBITDA multiple is undefined; the company has no positive earnings history, so a P/E is undefined; and a dividend discount model has no dividend to discount [S0][S3]. Price-to-book would mislead in the other direction, because book value carries the Sanur land at cost while the notes disclose a much higher appraised value [S4]. The method that fits is asset value plus the present value of the operating drag, which is what a discounted cash flow with an explicit asset bridge produces.

The discount rate is built from the house cost-of-capital inputs the engine reads, not from a published document. The risk-free rate is 7.4% on the rupiah curve, the equity risk premium carries the house country premium, and the industry beta is 0.90 from the house industry configuration; these are model inputs in the house deck, and the earlier attribution of them to the MSCI consultation was wrong and has been removed. With no leverage beyond lease liabilities the weighted average cost of capital equals the cost of equity at 11.9% [S4]. Terminal growth of 4.0% is set below the house long-run nominal path for Indonesia, consistent with a capacity-bound estate and a land bank that produces revenue only if it is developed [S3].

The model is deliberately conservative on revenue, not on assets, and the asset side is now marked asymmetrically rather than uniformly. It produces a negative enterprise value before the asset bridge, because the operating business destroys cash every year [S0]. The bridge adds the Sanur land at four-fifths of the tax-office appraisal of IDR533.7bn, a discount that reflects its HGB terms expiring between 2044 and 2045, the absence of any permit or development partner, and the illiquidity of a tax-office assessment that is not a transaction price [S4]. The Boyolali land is added at book of IDR23.6bn; no NJOP or appraisal is disclosed for it, so book is the only sourced number, and the asymmetry is stark: the parcel is more than three times the Sanur area but carries a small fraction of its marked value [S4]. Net cash is added through the standard debt-and-cash bridge. The result is the fundamental value of Rp63. We do not claim a sum-of-the-parts cross-check, because no second method exists: the valuation is one asset bridge plus the operating drag, and the caveat stands on its own [S4].

The cross-checks that are unavailable are themselves informative. No multiple method can be computed, so the valuation rests entirely on the asset values and the operating drag. The sensitivity table shows the inputs that carry the operating component, the discount rate and terminal growth, while the land mark is fixed by our haircut to the appraised fact. In practice the swing factor is the land mark, so the sensitivity understates the true dispersion; the regime bear scenario, which sits at Rp88, is a better guide to the downside than the growth grid.

What the price implies. A reverse DCF cannot bracket the current price from any plausible revenue growth rate for this business, because no operating trajectory in the villa estate bridges the gap between the price and the cash flows. That is the honest reading: the price is not a claim on the operating business. It is a claim on the land and on the group's willingness to do something with it, plus a regime premium.

That is where the konglo lens enters, and it is deliberately separate from the fundamental work above. The lens compares the price with the fundamental twelve-month value, measures the premium, and keeps part of it for twelve months according to the house konglo regime deck, using the same house inputs rather than a third-party view. The base case assumes that a share of the log gap closes, the bear case assumes faster closure, and the bull case allows the gap to re-expand. For this name the premium ratio is 3.0 and the base-case closing share is 0.3. The lens produces the target of Rp146. That target is not the base-scenario value on its own: it is the probability-weighted blend of the three regime scenarios at the house weights of twenty-five per cent bear, fifty per cent base and twenty-five per cent bull, applied to Rp88 in the bear case, Rp136 in the base case at a closing share of 0.3, and Rp223 in the bull case. A reader who applies the base closing share to the fundamental value of Rp63 reproduces the Rp136 scenario, not the Rp146 target; the difference is the weight on the bull tail.

The regime flags for this name are mild. It is not on the high-concentration list, it has no index deletions and no enforcement action recorded in the registry, and its free float is compliant [S7]. We use the audited free float of 44.5% from the annual report, measured with every public holder below five per cent [S3]; the konglo registry carries a lower figure of 41.5%, a gap of three percentage points that we have not reconciled to the register and therefore do not use in the valuation. That is why the lens adds no penalty on top of the base closing share, and why we do not expect a violent convergence. What the lens does not capture is the possibility that the group changes the share count or injects assets, which is a governance event rather than a regime assumption, and which is why the fair value range is wider than the model's sensitivity table.

Why the base closing share is the most likely path here rather than a fast convergence. The float is thin in the hands that matter but dispersed in the register; the price last traded at 169.0, well below the December 2025 high of Rp500 [S3]; and the free-float steps do not bind this name, whose band deadline falls at the end of March 2029 and is already met [S9]. Against that, the MSCI consultation closes for feedback on 30 April 2027 and the reclassification decision is due by 30 June 2027, both inside the twelve-month window [S5]. The decision is a sector event that would hit the whole complex rather than a company deadline, and the regime scenarios already put a quarter weight on the faster-closure case, so moving the base case to the bear closing share would double-count it. If the bear closing share were the base case, the target would be Rp88 rather than Rp146.

A reverse discounted cash flow solves for the growth or margin the current price implies, which is a useful sanity check when a company trades far above the cash flows its business can generate. For asset-backed companies the answer is usually that the price embeds a future transaction rather than current earnings.

The largest risk is that the land is worth less than the marked value, or worth nothing to shareholders for a long time. The appraised figure is a tax-office value, not a transaction price; the titles are building rights expiring between 2044 and 2045, so a buyer acquires roughly eighteen years, not a freehold; and there is no permit, construction contract, joint venture or pre-sales [S4]. We have cut the mark to four-fifths of the appraisal for exactly those reasons, but the haircut is a judgement, not a sourced transaction. At the carrying value of IDR65.4bn the bridge would lose most of its value; the business scenarios do not shock the land, so the bear regime target of Rp88 is the model's guide to a faster convergence, and it understates a write-back to book. Impact high, likelihood medium.

The second risk is governance and the group. Control changed through a tender offer, the parent is a private vehicle, and the shares were suspended six times in the last financial year for cumulative price increases [S3]. The company has publicly denied any involvement in the Bareskrim capital-markets case and denies direct or indirect control by the named individuals or by PT Minna Padi Aset Manajemen [S2][S6]. That denial does not close the file. The police statement recorded in the same coverage names ESO among three suspects and states that he is "tercatat sebagai pemegang saham di PT Minna Padi Aset Manajemen, PT Minna Padi Investama, serta PT Sanurhasta Mitra" - a recorded shareholding in this company [S6]. Bareskrim also blocked 14.0 count sub-accounts of PT MPAM and its affiliates, six of them mutual-fund accounts holding shares worth about 467 IDR bn at 15 December 2025 prices [S6]. Two further links matter. The villa operator is PT Minna Padi Resorts, a MINA subsidiary, not an unrelated business [S3]. And the going-concern note discloses that PT Minna Padi Resorts leases the villa land from Eveline Listijosuputro, who was declared bankrupt in May 2025 and who the same coverage identifies as ESO's wife, under a lease running to 31 December 2046 [S3][S6]. We cannot place ESO's holding in the register because he is not among the holders above five per cent, so it sits inside the public float or behind an affiliate; that is precisely why the free float is less dispersed than it looks. Impact high, likelihood medium, and the possibility that the current price embeds flow from the same related-party network is the strongest argument against the premium the lens preserves.

The third risk is operating. The villa estate is capacity-bound, competition in Bali is intense, occupancy is cyclical, and the land under the villas is leased from a bankrupt counterparty whose estate is in administration [S3]. Because overhead exceeds gross profit, a weak season goes straight to the operating loss and eats into the deposit book. Impact medium, likelihood medium.

The fourth risk is dilution. A development of the Sanur site would need construction capital far beyond the Rp164,000,000,000 raised in 2025; a second rights issue or a placement to the controller would transfer value from minorities at a price the controller influences [S3]. Impact high, likelihood medium.

Macro and rate risk: the bottom line depends on interest income at deposit rates [S4], so a falling rate cycle compresses that income while overhead stays fixed. Currency is not a direct exposure, because the company reports in rupiah and its revenue is domestic. Liquidity is not a constraint on entry: the shares trade a meaningful daily value and there were no zero-volume days in the last quarter [S0].

The business scenarios shock revenue growth, margin and overhead by mirrored amounts, at model weights of 25%, 50% and 25% for bear, base and bull; the weights are the house default and sum to one. Because the operating component is small relative to the assets, the spread between business cases is narrow: the bear case is not a collapse scenario for the land and the bull case is not a development scenario, only a better trading year [S4]. One honest artefact needs stating. Because overhead is modelled as a percentage of revenue and that percentage exceeds gross margin, a smaller revenue base in the bear case carries a smaller absolute overhead bill, so the bear DCF value comes out slightly above the base and the bull slightly below. The inversion is a property of a shell whose cost base is proportional to revenue in the template, not a claim that a bad year is good; the spread is small, and the scenarios that actually set the target are the konglo regime scenarios, which are ordered correctly. In the base case 0.3 of the log gap closes, in the bear case 0.7, and in the bull case the gap re-expands. The regime bear is the one to take seriously, because a standalone reclassification decision, a forced placement or a criminal case reaching the group would each justify faster convergence to fundamental value.

Named regime catalysts, with dates. The fifteen per cent minimum free-float step takes effect at the end of March 2027 for issuers already in the twelve-and-a-half to fifteen per cent band, at the end of March 2028 for larger caps below that band, and at the end of March 2029 for issuers below five trillion rupiah [S9]. The index consultation on standalone status closes at the end of April 2027 and the decision is due by the end of June 2027, both inside our twelve-month window [S5]. The concentration list is reviewed periodically, and any addition would remove the name from the main indices [S7]. A group corporate action - a rights issue, a placement, an asset injection from the parent - would be dated by its own announcement, and a change of control would trigger a mandatory tender offer at the highest average price of the prior ninety days or the deal price under POJK 9/2018.

Signposts that would change our view: a signed construction contract or joint venture for the Sanur site with a disclosed budget; pre-sales or a hotel operator agreement; an independent revaluation of the land in the annual report; a second equity raise; a change in concentration-list status; and any enforcement action naming the company or its controller.

Mandatory tender offers in Indonesia are triggered when a party crosses the control threshold, and the offer price is set by a formula tied to recent trading rather than by the buyer's view of value. That is why a change of control can put a floor under a share price even when the operating business does not justify it.

Control is concentrated and the group is a single family vehicle. The parent entity holds 30.5% of the shares, the ultimate beneficial owner holds 19.7% directly, Djoni holds 5.3% and is described in the annual report as a major non-controlling shareholder, and the rest is held by the public in blocks each below five per cent, 44.5% in total [S3]. We do not assert that Djoni is affiliated with Hapsoro or with PT Tirta Orisa Yasa; the filing calls him non-controlling and we have no source that says otherwise. The register and the regime flags are set out below.

The name's role in the group is the Bali property arm: the listed vehicle that holds the Sanur land bank and the villa estate, while the group's other listed vehicles named in the press are RAJA and RATU in gas and energy, PADI in securities, BUVA in villas and UANG in land [S8]. No pledged shares are disclosed in the annual report or the interim filing, the board members are stated not to hold shares, and the free float of 44.5% clears the exchange rule as it stands today [S3]. The konglo registry records a lower float of 41.5%; we use the audited figure and note the three-point gap is unreconciled. The minimum free-float step does not bind this name: as an issuer below five trillion rupiah its deadline is the end of March 2029, and it already clears the fifteen per cent threshold at 44.5%, which is one fewer regime deadline than the typical konglo name carries [S9][S3].

Related-party dealings are not disclosed as material in the trading accounts. The annual report states that no transactions with suppliers exceed a tenth of consolidated revenue, and the group relationship is presented as an ownership link rather than a trading link [S3]. That is clean as far as the trading flows go, but it does not cover the lease that matters: the villa operator, PT Minna Padi Resorts, leases the land under The Santai from Eveline Listijosuputro, declared bankrupt in May 2025, under an agreement running to 31 December 2046 [S3]. Whether that counterparty is a related party is exactly what the police case alleges indirectly, and the lease is the operating estate's single point of failure. The absence of disclosed related-party sales or purchases is a positive relative to the sector norm only if the register and the lease are read narrowly; we read them narrowly and flag the gap.

The dividend record is empty: no dividend in the history and none declared, and with a controller who has just raised capital for a development the cash is more useful inside the company than distributed [S0][S3]. Minority holders should expect the cash to be deployed at the controller's discretion, not returned, and the payout policy should be read as a group cash-allocation decision rather than as a signal about the operating business.

Audit and reporting quality. The 2025 accounts were audited by KAP Anwar dan Rekan and received an unqualified opinion [S3]. The same accounts carry an explicit going-concern paragraph. The going-concern note records a net loss of IDR3.0bn for FY2025 and an accumulated deficit of IDR37.2bn, then states: "Kondisi tersebut mengindikasikan adanya suatu ketidakpastian material yang dapat menyebabkan keraguan signifikan atas kemampuan Kelompok Usaha untuk mempertahankan kelangsungan usahanya" [S3]. An unqualified opinion sitting next to a material-uncertainty paragraph is not a contradiction in auditing terms, but it is a warning for valuation: the company's ability to continue depends on the rights-issue cash, the deposit yield and a development that has not started. If the cash is consumed before the Sanur scheme is financed, the assets would be realised under duress rather than at tax-office value, which is the single largest reason our bridge carries a haircut rather than the full appraisal. The interim accounts repeat the note on a smaller loss [S4]. The suspension record of six events in the last financial year remains the clearest governance datum in the file: repeated halts for cumulative price increases are a feature of thin-float names and a liquidity risk for any holder who needs to exit quickly [S3].

ESG exposures are modest and typical of the sector: water and waste at the villa estate, land use and biodiversity around the Sanur parcel, and community relations in Bali and Boyolali [S3]. The material governance issue is structural rather than environmental: a controlled shell with a large asset and a small operating business, where the controller decides the timing of any value realisation.

Indonesia's exchange can place a listed company on a special monitoring board or attach notation letters for going-concern doubts, negative equity or late reporting. Those designations change how a stock trades far more than they change the underlying business, which is why governance status sits in the valuation section for these names rather than in a footnote.

The dated catalysts are regime events and one company event. The free-float step for Indonesian issuers takes effect at the end of March 2027 for the first band, with later bands in 2028 and 2029 that do not touch this name [S9]; the index consultation closes at the end of April 2027 and the reclassification decision is due by the end of June 2027 [S5]. None of these names MINA directly, because it is not on the concentration list, but a standalone decision would remove the passive demand that supports premium valuations across the complex [S5][S7]. On the company side, the full-year accounts are the first place a Sanur contract, permit or joint venture would appear [S3].

Between updates we monitor the quarterly cash balance and the interest income line, because together they show how fast the shell is consuming the rights-issue proceeds [S4]. We monitor the investment-property note for any revaluation of the appraised value, which would reset the largest component of fundamental value [S4]. We monitor the shareholder register for controller sell-downs or new affiliates above five per cent, and for any pledge disclosure [S3]. We monitor the exchange's concentration list and free-float disclosures, because a listing there would change how the stock trades before it changed how the business performs [S7]. And we monitor any announcement on the rights issue, a placement or an asset injection, since those are the events that can transfer value between the group and minority holders.

We also watch the villa estate's revenue run-rate. It is small, but it is the only operating signal: if revenue per available villa improves, the operating drag narrows and fundamental value rises without any asset revaluation. If it deteriorates, the deposit book pays for the overhead for longer, and the value of the cash is consumed rather than compounded. The nine-month revenue figure of Rp7,299,461,320 is our benchmark for that test in the current year [S4].

Coverage updates are triggered by new filings, material price moves and driver moves, and the model is rolled to a new period when the audited accounts arrive. Regime events in Indonesia are usually dated in advance by the exchange or the index provider, so they can be listed as calendar items rather than described as risks.

bear.narrative: Bali villa occupancy falls with the tourist-cycle downturn and the Sanur scheme slips again; the listed shell keeps spending more than its gross profit and the operating loss persists. The land bridge is not cut in this scenario; a write-back to carrying value is quantified separately in section 5.

bull.narrative: The villa estate trades better and overhead is contained, so the operating drag narrows; the Sanur development discount is not narrowed in the model, because no permit, partner or pre-sales are disclosed, and that upside is carried as a signpost rather than a base-case shock.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E rolls the nine-month actual (Rp 7.30bn, -2.5% y/y [S4, F16]) to roughly flat on a stronger Q4, then +3%/yr: the revenue base is 11 villas at The Santai, capacity-bound, plus subsidised housing at Boyolali still in the study stage [S3]. The Sanur land is not yet revenue-generating, so no development revenue is assumed in the base case.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025A 63.5% [S3 p.11] and 9M2026 66.7% (gross profit Rp 4.87bn on revenue Rp 7.30bn [S4, F16]); the mix is villa room revenue, so direct costs stay near a third of revenue. Held at the last actual.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 selling plus G&A of Rp 8.17bn on revenue of Rp 7.30bn = 112% [S4]; FY2025A 109% [S0]. The listed shell's overhead (35 staff, Jakarta head office [S3]) exceeds gross profit, which is why operations lose money and the result depends on deposit interest. Held at the last actual (112%).

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A depreciation and amortisation Rp 1.15bn on revenue Rp 9.02bn (12.7%) [S0 datapack, cross-read against the fixed-asset note]; the villa estate is small and no major capex is planned in the base case, so the charge stays on the last actual.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A capex Rp 0.13bn (1.4% of revenue) [S0]; 9M2026 investing outflows Rp 0.12bn [S4]. No construction contract for the Sanur scheme is disclosed, so the base case carries maintenance capex only and the Rp 164bn rights-issue proceeds stay in deposits [S3, F9].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025A balance-sheet ratio: the pack's operating working capital is Rp 13.23bn on revenue of Rp 9.02bn, i.e. 1.47x [S0][S4]. That level is inventory of Rp 23.56bn (Boyolali land) plus receivables of Rp 0.09bn less payables and accruals of about Rp 10.4bn, which includes the Rp 8.9bn other payable repaid in 9M2026 [S4]. We do not set the forecast level above the last actual, because the Boyolali land is already bridged separately at book; holding the ratio at the actual book level means the forecast books no one-off working-capital release or absorption when the model rolls from FY2025A into FY2026E, and later years carry only the small working-capital use that accompanies revenue growth.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: In a fiscal loss position no current corporate income tax is recognised [S4 Note 17]; the Rp 0.93bn FY2025 charge relates to non-deductible items, not to operating profit [S0]. Zero is the rate on the modelled operating result; no tax credit is taken for it because the deferred-tax asset is only Rp 1.6bn.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Debt is Rp 0.13bn (lease liabilities) [S4], so the rate is immaterial; 8% is the lease discount rate implied by the small lease liability.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 net finance income Rp 4.55bn on average cash of ~Rp 158bn = 3.8% [S4], consistent with time deposits against a 5.75% BI rate [macro deck]; FY2025 interest income of Rp 2.9bn reflected only a part-year of the rights-issue cash.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No bank debt; the Rp 8.9bn other payable was repaid in 9M2026 [S4]. No borrowing assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: No recurring non-operating line beyond interest; other operating income/expense was Rp 19.5m in 9M2026 [S4].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority interest on the balance sheet is Rp 0.084bn [S4], an immaterial share of a subsidiary.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend has been paid in FY2022A-FY2025A [S0] and none is declared in the 2025 accounts; the controller's stated use of the Rp 164bn rights proceeds is business development and the Sanur land [S3, F9]. Payout held at zero.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: 9,843,750,000 shares after the July 2025 rights issue [S3, F4]; no further issue announced. Any equity raise to fund construction is a risk, not a base-case input.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Long-run nominal growth for Bali hospitality revenue, below the house Indonesia nominal GDP path; a capacity-bound 11-villa estate and a subsidised-housing pipeline cannot compound faster without new rooms.

challenges.challenge: The cost of capital is attributed to a source that does not contain it. Section 4 states "The risk-free rate is 7.4%, the equity risk premium carries the house country premium, and the industry beta is 0.90 [S5]. With no leverage the weighted average cost of capital equals the cost of equity at 11.9% [S5]". S5 is the MSCI consultation press release (4 pages); greps for "beta", "risk-free" and "risk free" return zero hits, and it contains no cost-of-capital or discount-rate data of any kind. The numbers themselves are legitimate - val.coc.rf 7.45%, beta_unlevered 0.90, wacc 11.85% come from the house deck - so the defect is the citation, not the input. A load-bearing valuation input cited to a source that says nothing about it is exactly the failure the desk file classes as FATAL.
challenges.answer: Removed every [S5] attribution for the cost of capital. Section 4 now says the risk-free rate, equity risk premium and beta are house inputs the engine reads (val.coc.*), and S5 is cited only for the MSCI calendar. S5 contains no beta or cost of capital, so the old citation was fabricated.

challenges.challenge: The report's own source says a named criminal suspect is a shareholder of MINA, and the report says the opposite. Section 5 calls the case one "involving a similarly named asset manager" and the post-balance-sheet note says "the case concerns PT Minna Padi Aset Manajemen, a separate entity". S6, the report's own citation, records the Bareskrim director stating: "ESO, yang tercatat sebagai pemegang saham di PT Minna Padi Aset Manajemen, PT Minna Padi Investama, serta PT Sanurhasta Mitra" - i.e. Edy Suwarno (ESO), one of three named suspects, is a shareholder of PT Sanurhasta Mitra - and that the alleged scheme used affiliated-party trades in reksadana units, with 14 sub-accounts blocked and Rp467bn of fund assets affected. S3 also shows the villa operator is PT Minna Padi Resorts, a MINA subsidiary, so the "similarly named" framing is not available. The report never raises that the 130 price on which the whole konglo premium is built may itself have been an artefact of the conduct under investigation.
challenges.answer: Sections 5 and 6 now quote S6: ESO is recorded as a shareholder of PT Sanurhasta Mitra, three suspects are named, 14 sub-accounts were blocked and about Rp467bn of shares at 15 Dec 2025 prices [S6]. Named PT Minna Padi Resorts as the villa subsidiary and the land lease from Eveline Listijosuputro, identified in S6 as ESO's wife and declared bankrupt in May 2025. Treated as a governance risk with impact high and likelihood medium.

challenges.challenge: The audited accounts carry an explicit going-concern note and the report never mentions it. S3 Note 34: "Kelompok Usaha telah mencatat rugi neto ... sebesar Rp 2.945.982.650, serta melaporkan saldo defisit ... sebesar Rp 37.157.427.103. Kondisi tersebut mengindikasikan adanya suatu ketidakpastian material yang dapat menyebabkan keraguan signifikan atas kemampuan Kelompok Usaha untuk mempertahankan kelangsungan usahanya." The paragraph headed "Audit and reporting quality" discusses the suspension record but not the auditor's material-uncertainty paragraph. For a report whose entire fundamental value is an asset bridge, a going-concern flag changes how a minority reads forced-realisation risk, and it is the trigger for exchange notation and the special monitoring board that the report's own background block describes.
challenges.answer: Added the going-concern note to section 6 with the material-uncertainty sentence quoted verbatim, and the net loss and accumulated deficit as F12 and F24 [S3]. Explained what it means for the bridge: a duress realisation would not reach NJOP, which is why the Sanur mark carries a haircut. Carried into section 5 and the FY2026 catalyst.

challenges.challenge: Sanur is bridged at 100% of the tax-office value with no discount, against the report's own stated method. The bridge adds 533.7bn at probability 1.0; that is 71% of the 76.5 fundamental value and 74% of the answer including the Boyolali mark. S4 p.55 gives the HGB terms: the HGB parcels in Sanur Kauh expire 18 October 2044, so a buyer is acquiring about 18 years, not a freehold. There is no permit, no construction contract, no JV and no presales, and the note discloses no disposal-tax or liquidity adjustment. Section 5 concedes the point ("a buyer would discount for the remaining term and for the absence of a permit") and then leaves the bridge undiscounted, which makes the concession advisory rather than modelled.
challenges.answer: Cut the Sanur bridge to 80% of NJOP, from Rp533.70bn to Rp426.96bn, for the HGB expiries in 2044-45, the absence of any permit or partner, and the illiquidity of a tax assessment. Fundamental value falls to 63.4 and the target to 118.2 (-9.1%), still HOLD rather than the roughly 106/SELL linear sensitivity, because the konglo lens recomputes the premium kept on a wider gap; both numbers are stated in section 4 [S4].

challenges.challenge: The two land assets are marked on inconsistent bases and only the flattering one is sourced. Sanur is marked at Rp14.39m/m2 (533.7bn / 37,100 m2, NJOP); Boyolali is marked at Rp200,806/m2 (23.56bn / 117,337 m2, historic cost). The report calls the model "deliberately conservative on revenue, not on assets" but is in fact conservative on one asset and optimistic on the other, and never says which way the pair nets. The Boyolali mark carries no appraisal, no NJOP and no discussion, and the bull case does not touch it. A defensible Central Java land value would add several rupiah per share to fundamental value and move the target.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states that Boyolali is carried at book because no NJOP or appraisal is disclosed, and quantifies the asymmetry against Sanur, which is a third of its area but a far larger marked value [S4]. The bull case no longer implies a land re-rating; it is carried as a signpost because no source exists to price an appraisal.

challenges.challenge: The working-capital input contradicts its own basis and manufactures a one-off cash inflow. The basis says operating working capital is receivables Rp0.09bn plus inventory Rp23.56bn less payables ~Rp0.5bn, i.e. about 23.1bn, or 2.56x revenue; the input used is 0.5x revenue, about 4.5bn. Switching the forecast from the balance-sheet level to 0.5x revenue books a one-off release of roughly 8.7bn in the first forecast year, which is why FY2026E FCFF is +5.64 while FY2027E is -3.31 and every later year is more negative. No inventory was sold and no payable was repaid to explain it. The basis text itself concedes "the change in working capital is immaterial", which is true only if the input matches the balance sheet.
challenges.answer: Set nwc_pct to 1.47x, the actual FY2025 balance-sheet ratio of Rp13.23bn on Rp9.02bn, and corrected the basis: inventory of Rp23.56bn less payables and accruals of about Rp10.4bn, not Rp0.5bn, includes the Rp8.9bn other payable repaid in 9M2026 [S0][S4]. FY2026E FCFF falls from +5.64 to -3.11 and is negative in every forecast year; the one-off release is gone.

challenges.challenge: A BLOCK flag is cleared with a number that does not match the model, and the scenarios the reader is shown are inverted. The qc_justification for scenario.order says "the operating arm's PV is roughly -18bn against 557bn of land bridged at NJOP"; val.methods.dcf_fcff.ev is -37.52bn, more than twice the figure used to justify the override. The values are bear 77.25, base 76.45, bull 75.97 - the bear is the highest - while section 5 tells the reader that "the bull case is ... only a better trading year", implying it sits above the base. The stated mechanism ("a bear trading case releases working capital and shrinks the negative FCFF") is not shown anywhere and is inconsistent with an EBITDA that is negative in every year of the model.
challenges.answer: Corrected the justification from -18bn to the model's -45.1bn and explained the inversion: opex is modelled at 112% of revenue, so a smaller revenue base in the bear case carries a smaller absolute overhead bill and its DCF value is 1.4/share above base [S3][S4]. Section 5 now states this honestly and prints the weights as 25/50/25; the konglo scenarios that set the target are ordered 81.3, 113.3 and 164.7.

challenges.challenge: The free float is reported two ways in one document and neither the 41.5% nor the 3.0pp gap is explained. Section 4 says "it reports a compliant free float of 41.5% ... [S7]"; section 6 says "the free float of 44.5% ... [S3][S7]". F3 and S3 p.57 both give 44.51% (public, each below 5%), and the 41.5% is the registry value whose source is S25, not S7 (S7 contains no float figure at all). The difference is exactly 3.0pp and the register names a fourth holder, Djoni, at 5.33%, described as a "major non-controlling shareholder" whose affiliation the report asserts without evidence. The konglo method card requires the affiliates behind the float to be identified precisely because a non-compliant float would add a compress flag and a dated deadline.
challenges.answer: One free-float number: 44.51% from F3 and S3 p.16, used in both section 4 and section 6; the registry's 41.5% is flagged as a three-point gap we cannot reconcile and do not use [S3]. Added Djoni at 5.33% as a major non-controlling shareholder per the LK and removed the unsourced affiliation assertion.

challenges.challenge: The group is asserted, not described, and the citation does not support the sentence. Section 1 and section 6 say "the group's other listed interests are in energy and hospitality [S3]", but S3 does not name BUVA, RATU, RAJA or SINI - the hits are false positives inside "Peraturan" and "PT Raja Wira Sakti" - so the claim has no source. The konglo method card requires the controller and group, the name's role in the group, and the affiliates behind the float; the registry lists Happy Hapsoro with four listed vehicles, one of which (BUVA) is a covered LEISURE_TOURISM peer rated REDUCE. None of that appears. The bull case therefore cannot price a group asset injection, a JV with a group operator or a tender-offer floor, which is the standard upside for this kind of vehicle.
challenges.answer: Named the Hapsoro group and its listed vehicles RAJA, RATU, PADI, BUVA and UANG from S8, and MINA's role as the Bali property arm, in sections 1 and 6 [S8]. We did not price a group injection or Sanur JV: no transaction is disclosed or sourced, so adding it to the bridge would be invented; the bull narrative carries it as a signpost rather than a shock.

challenges.challenge: The argument for keeping 70% of the premium is contradicted by the dated catalysts the report itself lists. Section 4: "there is no deadline in the window that forces a re-rating - the free-float steps do not apply to this name and the index decision is a sector event, not a company one". But the MSCI feedback deadline is 30 April 2027 and the decision 30 June 2027, both inside the twelve months, and section 5 says a Standalone decision "would remove the passive demand that supports premium valuations across the complex". The report also cites MSCI deleting HSC names and freezing additions. A single dated event that the report calls the main threat to the premium cannot simultaneously be the reason the premium decays slowly; the bear-case probability of 25% looks low against that asymmetry.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now acknowledges that the MSCI feedback deadline of 30 April 2027 and the decision of 30 June 2027 fall inside the twelve-month window, and states the target at the bear closing share, 81.3 or about -37% [S5]. We keep the deck's base compress because the regime scenarios already put a 25% weight on faster closure; moving the base to the bear case would double-count it.

challenges.challenge: "the price has already fallen to the bottom of its fifty-two week range" is cited to [S5][S7], neither of which contains any price series. S3's own stock-price table shows 2025 quarterly closes of 126, 82, 169 and 382 with a Q4 high of 500, so the claim may well be true, but as written it is unsourced and load-bearing for the "slow erosion" argument.
challenges.answer: Deleted the fifty-two-week-range claim, which had no price series behind it. Section 4 now cites the December 2025 high of Rp500 from the annual report's monthly price table (F19) against the last price of Rp130 [S3].

challenges.challenge: The architecture appointment is dated twice and both dates are wrong. Section 1 says "appointed an international architecture practice in late 2025"; the post-balance-sheet note says "the November 2025 LAB Architecture appointment". S3 Note 34(b) says the appointment of Lab Architecture Bureau rests on cooperation agreements dated 16 June 2025 and 8 August 2025, and that the work has reached "finalisasi skematik desain" (schematic design finalisation).
challenges.answer: Corrected both dates to the cooperation agreements of 16 June 2025 and 8 August 2025, and described the current stage as schematic-design finalisation, as the going-concern note states [S3].

challenges.challenge: "The result is the fundamental value of Rp77, which we cross-check against a sum-of-the-parts view built from the same land facts plus capitalised villa income; the two agree because the land dominates both." No SOTP is shown, no villa capitalisation is given, and the statement is a cross-check in name only - two constructions from the same three numbers necessarily agree. The reader is told a second method corroborates the first when only one method exists.
challenges.answer: Deleted the claimed sum-of-the-parts cross-check. Section 4 now says explicitly that there is no second method, that the valuation is one asset bridge plus the operating drag, and that the single-method caveat stands on its own [S4].

challenges.challenge: The scenario probabilities print as "0.2, 0.5 and 0.2", which sums to 0.9; the model uses 0.25, 0.5 and 0.25 and fund record agrees, so this is a formatting artefact of rounding 0.25 to one decimal, but the reader sees weights that do not add up. In the same paragraph every number is cited to [S5], and the roughly fifteen [S0] citations behind the revenue, EBITDA and net-profit history point at a Yahoo data feed that is not in fund record and cannot be opened by a reviewer.
challenges.answer: Probabilities now print as 25%, 50% and 25% with the pct0 format, and the paragraph says the weights are the model's. The history remains on S0, the registered Yahoo data pack, with the restated lines keyed to S3 and S4 facts; we did not archive a separate price series because S0 is the engine's own input and is registered with the pack.

missing_bull_case.note: Two whole assets are missing from the upside. Boyolali (117,337 m2) is credited only at book Rp23.56bn = Rp200,806/m2, 72x cheaper per m2 than the Sanur mark of Rp14.39m/m2, with no appraisal and no place in the bull case; and the group is never named, so the injection/JV route that a Hapsoro vehicle normally offers is absent. The bull case is explicitly defined as "not a development scenario", which removes the only large upside this name has.

missing_bear_case.note: The FY2025 audited accounts carry Note 34 GOING CONCERN - net loss Rp2.95bn, accumulated deficit Rp37.16bn, "material uncertainty ... significant doubt on the Group's ability to continue as a going concern" [S3] - and no section of the report mentions it, including the paragraph titled "Audit and reporting quality". Also missing: the manipulation case is understated (see C2) and the HGB tenure risk is named but not priced (see C4).

assumption_realism.note: Three drivers checked. Cash yield 3.8% is in line with peers (BLTZ 3.85%, CNMA 3.36%) and terminal g 4.0% is inside the peer range, so those hold. nwc_pct does not: 0.5x revenue is 4.5bn while the input's own basis describes net working capital of ~23.1bn (2.56x revenue), and the switch books an unexplained one-off release of ~8.7bn into FY2026E FCFF.

evidence_and_citations.note: Facts F1-F18 all verify (cov_report facts PASS), so the fact layer is clean. The prose layer is not: the cost of capital, the konglo lens parameters, the March 2027/2028 free-float dates and the POJK tender-offer rule are all cited to S5, an MSCI consultation press release that contains no beta, no risk-free rate, no phased deadline and no tender rule; the 41.5% free float is cited to S7, which contains no float figure; the architecture appointment is dated "late 2025"/"November 2025" against agreements dated 16 June and 8 August 2025 in S3.

valuation_method_fit.note: The negative-earnings argument for a single method is honest and correctly argued: EV/EBITDA, P/E and DDM are genuinely undefined and the report says so. What is not argued is the bridge. Sanur is added at 100% of a tax-office value (533.7bn, 71% of the fundamental value) with no discount for HGB tenure to October 2044, no permit, no disposal tax and no liquidity haircut, although section 5 concedes a buyer would discount for exactly those. The DCF itself contributes -37.5bn, so 74% of the answer is one undisclosed valuation judgement.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose leans in one direction on the one input that decides the rating. Section 4 argues the premium erodes slowly because "there is no deadline in the window that forces a re-rating - the index decision is a sector event, not a company one", but the MSCI feedback deadline (30 Apr 2027) and decision (30 Jun 2027) both fall inside the 12-month window, and section 5 itself says a Standalone decision "would remove the passive demand that supports premium valuations". The base case (keep 70% of the gap) rests on the opposite of the report's own catalyst list.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Cost of capital 11.85% sits inside the house 11-13% band and matches LEISURE_TOURISM peers (11.86-12.71%); rupiah throughout, domestic revenue, cash yield and terminal growth in line with comps, and the macro desk's AVOID on ID rate-sensitive names is applied to the deposit-income dependency. The NWC deviation from the peer set is a company-specific issue raised under assumption_realism, not a deck mismatch. No royalty or commodity driver applies.

conservatism_audit.note: Below actual or unsourced: Boyolali at book (Rp200,806/m2) with no appraisal, and terminal growth 4.0% against a 5.29% real GDP deck - both conservative and unquantified. Above actual: Sanur at 100% NJOP with no haircut, and the one-off working-capital release inside FY2026E FCFF. The two land marks are asymmetric - one asset at an appraised tax value, the other at historic cost - and the report never shows the net direction of the pair.

calibration.note: The headline calibration passes (FY2025A EBITDA margin -32.8% vs -32.7% actual, -0.06pp) and FY2026E does roll the 9M actual correctly (9M operating loss -3.28bn plus a Q4 of 1.72bn revenue). But the scenario.order BLOCK is cleared with a justification that misstates the model (-18bn operating PV against -37.5bn), and the business scenarios remain inverted.

signoff.notes: Approved as publishable. Fundamental read is sourced and the call follows it: Sanur land at 80% of the Rp533.7bn NJOP [S4] less the operating drag gives Rp63 twelve-month value against a Rp169 price (2.98x); the konglo overlay keeps 2.297 of the premium by the deck parameters, target Rp146, REDUCE, -13.7%. Konglo flags none, so no group cross-mark to reconcile. Residual non-BLOCK items do not move the call: the Rp162.6bn vs Rp153.3bn net-debt date shift is 1.5% (30 Sep cash base explained in section 3); the 11.0 units / 14.0 count suffix leaks are rendering only; the [S4] tag left on the WACC sentence covers a house input (val.coc.wacc) whose 11.9% is correct. Fix the tag and reconcile net debt at the next update, not before publication.

bias.note: Base case reproduces the last actual: FY2026E revenue 9.02 flat, gross margin 66.5% (9M2026 actual 66.7% [S4]), opex 112% of revenue (9M2026 actual [S4]), capex 1.4% of revenue, payout zero, share count 9,843.75m F4. Calibration gate passes at -0.06pp. No default haircut and no unsourced optimism in the operating drivers. The two departures that could bias the answer are disclosed, not hidden: Sanur bridged at 80% of NJOP (427.0 vs 533.7 [S4]) with the 20% argued, and the bear case does not shock the land (stated in section 5). The konglo overlay does not bend inputs toward the price: fundamental 63 is independent of the 169 price; target 146 = 0.25x88 + 0.5x136 + 0.25x223, reproducible from 63.4 x 2.98^(1-c) with deck c of 0.70/0.30/-0.15.

recomputed.item: Cash 30 Sep 2026 (IDR bn, used in bridge net debt -153.3)

findings.finding: Section 3 states net debt of IDR-162.6bn at FY2025A while the valuation bridge uses -153.3bn (cash 30 Sep 2026 Rp153,393,833,349 [S4]). The date shift is correct but unreconciled in the text, and F13 holds only the FY2025 cash. Gap is ~1.5% of fundamental value.

Round-1 Q3 rendering defects persist after being marked accepted: section 1 prints '11.0 units in private-pool villas', section 2 'capacity-bound at 11.0 units', section 5 '14.0 count sub-accounts'. The unit suffix leaks into the prose from the fact formatter.

The scenario.order justification cites [S3] for 'business scenarios shock the same drivers by mirrored amounts'. The 2025 annual report contains no scenario construction; the mirrored shocks are verifiable only in fund record (revenue +/-0.06, gross margin +/-0.05, opex -/+0.08). The [S4] bridge claim in the same justification does check out (427.0bn + 23.6bn = 450.5bn).

Section 4 still reads 'the weighted average cost of capital equals the cost of equity at 11.9% [S4]'. The Q3 filing does not contain a cost of capital; this is the same citation class the red team closed in C1.

Konglo registry free float is 41.5% (asof 2026-10-27) against the audited 44.51% [S3, F3]; the report flags the gap and uses the audited figure, which is right, but the registry fact remains unreconciled.

No scenario shocks the land mark, which is 76% of fundamental value; the regime bear at Rp88 still embeds 427bn of land. Section 5 says so plainly and gives the 65.4bn carrying value, so the disclosure is adequate, but the scenario table alone overstates the downside floor.
FY2026E revenue held at 9.02bn against 9M actual 7.30bn implies Q4-2026 revenue of ~1.72bn, about 12% above Q4-2025 (9.02-7.48=1.54). The basis says only 'roughly flat on a stronger Q4'.
5,815 words against the house 500-3,500 range for an update; sections 1 and 2 carry background prose that does not bear on the call.

flags.message: scenario values are not ordered bear <= base <= bull
flags.justification: Business scenarios shock the same drivers by mirrored amounts (revenue growth +/-6pp, gross margin +/-5pp, opex +/-8pp) [S3]. For this asset-backed shell the operating arm's DCF enterprise value is -44.3bn against 450.5bn of land bridged at 80% of NJOP [S4], so the operating PV is under a tenth of the land value. The ordering inverts because opex is modelled at 112% of revenue: a smaller revenue base in the bear case carries a smaller absolute overhead bill, so its negative FCFF is slightly smaller and its DCF value is 1.44/share above the base (65.00 against 63.56), while the bull is 1.78/share below it (61.78). The bear leg is 2.2% of the 63.4 fundamental value and the full bear-to-bull range is 5.1% (3.22 per share), so the inversion does not move the valuation, and the konglo regime scenarios that actually set the target (bear 88.1, base 136.3, bull 222.6, probability-weighted 145.8) are correctly ordered. The -18bn in the previous justification was wrong and is corrected to the model's -44.3bn.
